newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Amcor drops 15 pct EPS growth target.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Amcor drops 15 pct EPS growth target.

text.p: Paper and packaging group Amcor ltd said on Monday that it had dropped its target for 15 percent annual growth in earnings per share (EPS).

"We don't think, under present circumstances, that is a reasonable target, so we are not proposing to have that growth rate of 15 percent EPS as a target because we just think it is inappropriate and probably unacceptable and unachievable," said group managing director Don Macfarlane.
Instead, Amcor is considering a new target requiring the group to outperform Australia's top 25 industrial companies in terms of EPS growth.
Macfarlane cited difficult trading conditions at home and abroad, and a sustained low-inflation environment as reasons for ditching the 15 percent target.
"We have to condition ourselves to living in a different kind of environment, to living with low inflation," Macfarlane said, adding that low inflation inhibited scope for price rises.
Earlier, Amcor posted a lower net profit of A$338.8 million for the year to June 30, 1996, from A$359.7 million in 1994/95, and a 15.6 percent drop in pre-tax operating profit to A$519.7 million.
It kept its final dividend unchanged at 20 cents.
Amcor shares ended 12 cents lower at A$7.62.
